corridor.titleTemplate: Sending {amount} to {place} by stablecoin {marketPhrase}. The cheapest app {appPhrase}.
corridor.ledeTemplate: A stablecoin is a digital coin that stays near one dollar, such as USDT or USDC. We price buying one, sending it, and selling it, every hour. Today the cheapest app is {provider}, by its advertised price.
corridor.verdict1: Right now {amount} costs {marketCost} ({marketPct}) all in by stablecoin with a market order, and {appCost} ({appPct}) with the cheapest app, {provider}. The stablecoin route costs {diff} {moreOrLess}.

waterfall.capTemplate: Buying the stablecoin is {buyCost} of the {totalCost}. The dashed line is the cheapest app.
waterfall.gainNote: A bar to the left of that line means that step paid money back on this sample, not that it cost money.
waterfall.disclosure: This chart only counts what happens on the exchanges. Getting money into the first exchange, and getting it out to a bank account at the end, may cost more. This site has not measured that cost.

corridor.footerTemplate: Stablecoin bought on {onrampVenue} in {srcCcy}, sold on {offrampVenue} for {dst}, on each exchange's published fees. App prices are advertised prices, including first-transfer offers where shown. A limit order is an offer at a price you pick. We assume it fills at the best price currently offered on the exchange. Official rate from open.er-api.com. Negotiated corporate rates are not included.
